description: MARS: Junior Astronaut é um jogo interativo que simula uma missão a Marte. Jogadores gerenciam suporte de vida, radiação e um rover robótico para coletar dados e superar desafios. Junte-se a nós para criar uma experiência incrível de exploração espacial! Buscamos membros com habilidades em desenvolvimento de jogos, design de UI/UX e paixão por ciência espacial para tornar este projeto realidade.
summary: MISSION FORGE is an interactive space mission engineering simulator that integrates real NASA scientific data LOLA topography, DIVINER temperatures, and water-ice evidence at the Lunar South Pole to drive simulation decisions and outcomes. Users design a field explorer robot (power, mass, thermal, communications), validate the mission, and run field operations where every choice responds to real lunar conditions: permanent shadow, extreme thermal swings, and rugged terrain. NASA open data is downloaded, processed, and methodologically documented, distinguishing observational evidence from hypothesis and never inventing measurements. The game runs fully offline, making it accessible at schools and events without infrastructure. By turning raw datasets into a playable, decision-driven experience, MISSION FORGE democratizes planetary science literacy: anyone can understand why Lunar South Pole exploration demands careful engineering and test their own hypotheses against real data.
details:
What it does / how it works.

MISSION FORGE is a browser-based space mission engineering simulator. Players design a Lunar South Pole explorer robot (power, mass, thermal, communications), validate the design with a real calculation engine, and run field operations — where the deciding conditions come from actual NASA open data: terrain elevation and shading from the LOLA digital elevation model (LDEM_75S, 240 m/px), surface temperatures from the DIVINER thermal product (PRP South), and water-ice evidence from published measurements (LCROSS at Cabeus). Pipeline: raw data download → offline processing with Node.js scripts (JPEG2000 decoding, ×0.5 + 1,737,400 m scaling, JSON/PNG generation) → environment models (terrain, temperature, illumination, ice) → simulation engine → UI. Everything is bundled statically, so it runs fully offline.

Benefits.

Teaches genuine engineering concepts (power budget, thermal, mission risk) whose outcomes derive from real lunar data instead of invented numbers; turns raw, hard-to-use scientific datasets into an accessible, decision-driven experience; runs offline on any computer.

Intended impact.

Planetary science literacy in schools, museums, and hackathon events: people understand why the Lunar South Pole is hard — permanent shadow, extreme cold, hostile terrain — by testing their own hypotheses against real data.

Tools & technologies.

TypeScript, React 18, Vite, Three.js (3D terrain), Zustand (state), Vitest (tests), Node.js (data pipeline), OpenJPEG codec (JPEG2000 DEM decoding), custom PNG encoder, HTTP Range requests (selective extraction from the 604 MB Diviner PRP product). Data: NASA PDS (LOLA GDR, Diviner Derived1) and published literature (LCROSS; Paige et al. 2010).

Creative aspect.

Rigorous separation between visualization and science: the 3D scene never performs scientific calculations — it only displays values produced by documented models. Layered integration (topography → shading → solar power → thermal risk → ice evidence) makes every NASA data pixel change a gameplay decision. Scientific integrity as gameplay: the game explicitly labels observational evidence vs hypothesis and never fabricates measurements.

Team considerations.

Reproducibility (full pipeline versioned in scripts/), methodological documentation (docs/DATA_METHODOLOGY.md, SCIENCE_SOURCES.md, ASSETS_LICENSES.md), equitable access (offline, zero infrastructure cost), accuracy without sensationalism (simplified-data labels, corrected V2.0 sources), and performance (pre-processed, embedded data; no heavy runtime computation).
